seoTitle: Free EU VAT Number Format Validator
metaDescription: Check the format of EU VAT numbers by country prefix, one per line. Format only, no registry lookup. Free and runs in your browser.
intro: Paste EU VAT numbers one per line and see whether each matches the format used by its country prefix. This checks the pattern only, not registration.
why:
Invoicing forms, checkout pages and supplier imports all collect VAT numbers, and a lot of them arrive with the wrong shape: missing prefix, extra dots, a letter in the wrong place. Catching those before submission saves a failed lookup or a rejected invoice.

This tool normalises each line by removing spaces, dots and hyphens, reads the two-letter country prefix and tests the rest against that country's pattern. It supports the EU member prefixes, including EL for Greece. It is a first-pass format check. It does not call VIES, so it cannot confirm that a number is registered, active or belongs to the named company, and some countries have checksum rules that are not applied. Your data stays in the browser.
howTo: Paste VAT numbers into the box, one per line, each starting with the country prefix.
Read the result next to each number: format OK or wrong format for that country.
Verify important numbers against the official VIES service.

faq.q: Does this confirm a business is VAT registered?
faq.a: No. It only checks that the pattern fits the country. To confirm registration you need the European Commission's VIES service or your tax authority, which this page does not contact.

faq.q: How do I write Greece and Northern Ireland?
faq.a: Greece uses the prefix EL, not GR. Northern Ireland uses XI, which is not in this tool's list, so those numbers are reported as unknown prefix. Other non-EU prefixes are also flagged.
Yes. Spaces, dots and hyphens are removed before checking, so DE 123.456.789 is treated like DE123456789. The original text is still shown in the result.

faq.q: Why can a number pass but still be wrong?
faq.a: Format checks cannot detect a mistyped digit that keeps the right pattern. Several countries also use checksum digits that this tool does not verify, so treat OK as plausible, not proven.
